extracted.intended_audience: general news readership interested in corporate/crisis coverage
extracted.subtask_description: A news article covering a corporation's public response and leadership changes during a major crisis (here: BP and the Deepwater Horizon oil spill). Focus is on how executives communicate, who speaks for the company, and public/political reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forthcoming, direct answers to oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism arose because Hayward "refus[ed] to say whether BP made dangerous and risky decisions leading up to the spill" and repeatedly said he would "not draw any conclusions ... until investigations ... were completed." Rep. Eliot Engel: "You're really insulting our intelligence ... by not giving us any answers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to Congress, regulators, or the public during a crisis, provide clear, direct information where available; avoid repeatedly deferring to future investigations in a way that appears evasive. Acknowledge unknowns but give what factual answers can be responsibly provided to avoid the appearance of stonewalling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empathetic, non‑self‑centered public statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Hayward's comment "I'd like my life back" was described as infamous and part of the backlash against him for appearing self‑centered amid a disaster that killed 11 men and devastated communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft messaging that centers affected people and communities, expresses sympathy for victims, and avoids language that foregrounds executives' personal inconvenience. Tone matters — self‑focused remarks can inflame public and political reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate genuine commitment to safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Hayward asserted his commitment to safety, citing a past incident where an employee died and how that changed his views: leaders "must make the safety of all who work for them their top priority."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should show concrete commitment to safety (past actions, policies, memorial actions) and convey how the company is prioritizing prevention and protection. Statements about safety are stronger when supported by examples or steps being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an appropriate public face and organizational structure for response
rubrics_metrics.description: BP shuffled Hayward out of the spotlight and named managing director Robert Dudley to take over responding to the crisis; BP said Dudley would "lead a new organization 'to manage the long-term response once the spill is over.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider assigning a different spokesperson or leadership arrangement if the primary executive is under heavy criticism; appointing a crisis‑focused leader can signal seriousness and create clearer, more effective communications and long‑term response management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid minimizing language or phrasing that offends
rubrics_metrics.description: BP Chairman Carl‑Henric Svanberg was criticized after saying BP cares "about the small people" while apologizing — a remark that drew negative attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies and public remarks should be carefully worded to avoid diminutive or dismissive language. Test phrasing for unintended connotations; a clumsy apology can exacerbate reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be timely and consistent without overreliance on 'wait for investigations'
rubrics_metrics.description: Hayward repeatedly reiterated that he would not draw conclusions until investigations were completed, which frustrated Congress and observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance caution with the need for timely updates. Clearly communicate what is known now, what is being investigated, and when further information will be provided. Overuse of 'we must wait' can be perceived as evasive or unresponsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about leadership roles and backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes Dudley's U.S. nationality, compensation ($6.4 million), Amoco merger background, and Hayward's compensation ($14.3 million) and personal life details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure of who is leading the response, their qualifications, and relevant background can shape public perception. Transparency about leadership and organizational changes helps the public and stakeholders evaluate the company's capability to manage the crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept accountability and show willingness to change course
rubrics_metrics.description: Hayward was "excoriated" for his role and public statements; the company signaled a leadership shift in response to criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating accountability — through accepting responsibility where appropriate, making leadership changes, or altering response strategies — can mitigate reputational damage. Reactive changes should be accompanied by clear explanations of how actions will improve outcomes.
